features.name: Source tree
features.detail: Live source folder for the project.

features.name: Subjects store + matcher
features.detail: data/subjects.json holds {name, keywords[], enabled}. Seeded with the same nine-subject vocabulary TubeScout uses. Word-boundary regex matching tolerant of the obvious inflections (nomad/nomads, retire/retired); a title hit scores double a channel-name hit.

features.name: Subscription feed aggregator
features.detail: Per-host map of 'people I follow' pages for 11 platforms (YouTube /feed/subscriptions first-class). Background thread with per-site status, results interleaved round-robin and cached in data/subscriptions.json; every item tagged with matching subjects.

features.name: Subscribed-channel list
features.detail: YouTube /feed/channels read with the saved cookies into data/subscription_channels.json — each channel becomes a one-click browse button.

features.name: Logged-in static scrape
features.detail: fetch_html now sends the saved cookie file's cookies for the host. The scrape tier previously fetched anonymously, which made every logged-in listing page a sign-in prompt.

features.name: Alias suppression for feeds
features.detail: discover(allow_aliases=False) keeps homepage substitutions out of subscription fetches, so a TikTok For You grid can never be presented as 'from people you follow'.

features.name: Subs tab + Subjects settings
features.detail: The 📡 Subs pane has subject filter chips with counts, site and sort selectors, an on-subject-only toggle, a per-site pill row and background-job polling. Settings gains a Subjects editor. Browse and Subs share one card renderer.
